extractor.note: Partial pass over Chapter I, §§ 1-2, where the reduction is read into Biran's method.

coverage_note: Covers Chapter I, § 1 (the phenomenological presuppositions of Biranian ontology) and § 2 (the transcendental deduction of the categories). Chapters II and V also carry hits and are not covered.

units.claim: Biran's discovery of a second kind of observation is said to coincide with the phenomenological reduction and to be one with it.
units.quote: the moment of the discovery coincides with the phenomenological reduction, with which it is one

units.claim: The idea of the reduction is read in the movement by which Biranian thought opposes construction, theory, hypothesis and probability.
units.quote: The idea of such a reduction can also be read in the constant movement by which Biranian thought opposes everything that is construction, theory, hypothesis, probability

units.claim: The foundation of psychology is the sphere of absolute certainty in which transcendental inner experiences are accomplished, the sphere the reduction leads back to.
units.quote: that foundation is furnished by the sphere of existence where transcendental inner experiences are accomplished, the sphere of absolute certainty to which the reduction has led us back

units.claim: Theories of knowledge erected outside the sphere of certainty that is subjectivity have a content that can only fall under the phenomenological reduction.
units.quote: one has left the sphere of certainty that is subjectivity, one erects theories of knowledge whose content can only fall under the phenomenological reduction

units.claim: Biran subjects innateness to the reduction and recovers it within immanence, in the phenomenological transcendental ego.
units.quote: Biran subjects innateness to the reduction and recovers it in the sphere of immanence, endowed with its true sense

units.claim: The transcendental deduction of the categories is in reality a reduction, since to deduce a category is to reduce its being to what it originally and irreducibly is.
units.quote: The deduction is in reality a reduction: to deduce a category is to reduce its being to what it originally is, this time irreducibly.

units.term: phenomenological reduction of empiricism and positivism
units.claim: The reduction performed by empiricism and positivism holds only on the plane of transcendent being, where it shows there is no room for the idea of causality.
units.quote: The phenomenological reduction performed by empiricism and positivism is true on its own plane, that of transcendent being

units.claim: The Biranian reduction does not put the being of the world in question but circumscribes what in that being is original and genuinely certain.
units.quote: There is indeed a phenomenological reduction in Biranism, but unlike what some commentators on Husserl suppose, it does not put the being of the world in question; it seeks rather to circumscribe what in such being is original and enjoys genuine certainty.
